content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.3) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (sentiment < 0.1) — model ignores downside risk and fails to adjust for mean reversion.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term price drops — forecasts lag behind true price declines, especially in the first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings > 0.2), model overfits to recent highs/lows and fails to smooth out noise.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher prices — model assumes continuation of recent trends, ignoring structural mean reversion.
- If sentiment is consistently low over 3–5 days, model should reduce forecast slope and add downward bias to avoid “overconfident” upward drift.
- Model underestimates sharp downward moves after high sentiment peaks — fails to recognize sentiment-driven sell-off triggers.
- When sentiment is high but price is falling, model often ignores sentiment signal and continues upward bias — should adjust downward by 5–10% of forecasted value.
